verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents its own SDK, CLI, and build-extension system for writing tasks as plain TypeScript functions that can be triggered from your code, and community users describe replacing n8n-style GUI workflows with code-defined integrations. However, the evidence never documents a dedicated connector or private-integration framework, so building one means hand-writing task code rather than using a purpose-built connector model. missing for 10: explicit docs for a custom connector/integration framework, worked examples of building a private integration, a published OpenAPI spec (probes returned 404), and independent hands-on reports of building a connector specifically.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a custom connector or private integration with a documented developer platform, SDK, or CLI

citations.quote: Tasks are plain async/await functions with no workflow DSL, no determinism rules, and no execution time limit.
Build extensions allow you to hook into the build system and customize the build process or the resulting bundle and container image
use `new TriggerClient({...})` for each target instead of `configure()`
easily integrates with tools we use
